findings.title: UsernameForm calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() but only the one-argument overload exists
findings.body: `UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments. The only definition added to `UsernamePasswordForm` is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`. There is no no-arg overload in this class or its parent `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator`, so `UsernameForm` does not compile and the `services` module build fails. Either add a no-arg overload, or pass `context.getUser()` here. The no-arg form is probably what was intended, since this branch is only entered when the user is non-null.

findings.title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null, which disables passkeys on the initial login page
findings.body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns true only when `user != null`. Before this change, `authenticate()` and `challenge(context, error, field)` set up passkeys when the user was not yet identified (`context.getUser() == null`). With the new guard, the normal first-visit login, where no user is in the context, never calls `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm`. The conditional-UI attribute, challenge and rpId are not set, so passkey login is lost for the standard flow. The patch's own tests expect passkeys on the first page: the "username webauthn" autocomplete, `form#webauth`, and auto-login with a discoverable key. They would fail. The `user != null` condition should be dropped so passkeys are enabled whenever the realm has them enabled, for both fresh login and re-authentication.

findings.title: Passkey setup in authenticate() is skipped for a new login because of the user != null check
findings.body: The passkey setup was moved out of the `else` (user == null) branch so it also covers re-authentication. It is now gated by `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, which requires a non-null user. The effect is inverted. Re-authentication gets passkeys, but the first-time login, where `context.getUser()` is null, no longer does. The same inverted check is in the `challenge(context, error, field)` override (line 137). Error re-renders such as a bad username or a failed passkey on the first login page therefore also lose the conditional UI.

findings.title: shouldDisplayAuthenticators is not overridden alongside shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators
findings.body: `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` now returns false for conditional-UI login. `WebAuthnAuthenticator.shouldDisplayAuthenticators` is not overridden and still returns `context.getUser() != null`. During re-authentication (user set) the form therefore gets `SHOULD_DISPLAY_AUTHENTICATORS=true` and `IS_USER_IDENTIFIED=false`, but no `ALLOWED_AUTHENTICATORS` attribute. A template that renders the authenticator list under that flag may fail or render an empty list. The method is also missing `@Override`, so a signature mismatch would not be caught by the compiler.

findings.title: reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey comment does not match what is tested, and missing-element checks are weak
findings.body: The comment says the user has no passkey and passkeys should be hidden, but the test disables passkeys at the realm level (`setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(FALSE)`). It does not cover the case the name implies: passkeys enabled on the realm, user without a registered passkey. In that case `fillContextForm` still runs with a non-null user. The absence checks use `findElement(...)` inside `try/catch (Exception)`, which only passes because `findElement` throws. The `assertThat(..., nullValue())` can never pass if the element exists, so it is misleading. Use `findElements(...).isEmpty()` or `assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)`.
